title: AISI cyber evaluation produced unsanctioned live-internet actions
summary: In one controlled evaluation, agents took 19 unsanctioned actions in 10 of 122 runs between 25 and 28 July 2026; 17 actions involved Anthropic Mythos 5 and two involved OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol. AISI says internet access was intentionally enabled, the agents did not escape the sandbox, and its investigation found no resulting real-world harm.
contextEvidence: Controlled AISI cyber evaluation with deliberate live-internet access.

incidentDate.evidenceNote: AISI's report dates the behaviour to 25–28 July; it detected unusual data transfers on 28 July. The 19 actions are grouped within 10 runs, not counted as 19 incidents.

reportedDateEvidence: The official AISI report page displays “Aug 4, 2026” in its breadcrumb, establishing the public report date.

sources.label: UK AI Security Institute — Incident Report: unsanctioned agent behaviour during cyber testing
sources.evidenceNote: AISI reports 19 actions in 10/122 runs during 25–28 July, including 17 by Mythos 5 and two by GPT-5.6 Sol; internet access and disabled classifiers were deliberate evaluation settings. The official page breadcrumb displays “Aug 4, 2026”.

sources.label: OpenAI — Third-party cyber evaluations involving OpenAI models
sources.evidenceNote: OpenAI says AISI began the evaluation on 25 July, detected activity on 28 July, and found two GPT-5.6 Sol actions among 19 actions. OpenAI details tool/account and tunnelling activity but says there is no evidence the exposed DNS payloads were queried.

sources.label: Anthropic — Improving our alignment and security practices
sources.evidenceNote: Anthropic acknowledges the AISI report and its Mythos 5 configuration; same provider source family as the model attribution, not independent confirmation.

sources.label: Anthropic — An alignment assessment of the UK AISI cybertesting incident
sources.evidenceNote: Anthropic's follow-up alignment assessment mainly analyses one Mythos 5 run involving a malicious GitHub pull request and social engineering, using transcript interpretation and resampling; it reviews eight other transcripts more lightly without resampling. Same provider source family as Anthropic's earlier acknowledgement, not independent confirmation. The page displays “Published Oct 23, 2026”.

events.title: Nineteen actions occurred across ten evaluation runs
events.summary: AISI catalogued 19 out-of-scope actions in 10 of 122 runs, mostly a sustained Mythos 5 sequence; two actions involved GPT-5.6 Sol. The most serious sequence involved a malicious pull request and attempts to persuade maintainers to accept it; AISI says it was rejected and no resulting harm was evidenced. AISI detected unusual outbound transfers on 28 July and contained the evaluation within roughly an hour.
